DDInter1791.mechanism: INTERVAL: Methylxanthines (e.g., caffeine, theophylline) are nonspecific, competitive antagonists of adenosine receptors. As such, they may interfere with the pharmacologic effects of adenosine and other adenosine receptor agonists such as dipyridamole and regadenoson. There have been case reports of patients receiving theophylline who required higher than normal dosages of adenosine for the treatment of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia.
